payload.name: Preserve recommendations when merging into preference memories
payload.description: When extraction or CRUD handles a candidate whose source message contains a recommendation or suggestion, keep the speech-act context distinct from mere personal preference and do not let an UPDATE/MERGE strip it.
content: During extraction, if the source explicitly recommends or suggests an entity, keep the speech-act verb (e.g., 'recommends', 'suggested') in the candidate content; do not collapse it into a bare preference like 'enjoys X'.

During CRUD, before performing an UPDATE or MERGE into an existing memory, check whether the new evidence contains a recommendation distinct from an enjoyment/preference claim. If so, preserve the recommendation explicitly (e.g., 'recommends X as ...' or 'suggested X for ...') even when merging into a preference memory, and avoid rewording it into only an enjoyed-item list.

solves: Construction often merges a new candidate containing an explicit recommendation or suggestion into an existing preference memory, converting 'recommends X as great' into 'enjoys X' and silently dropping the speech-act fact. This happens in any domain (games, books, movies, restaurants, products) whenever a source message endorses something. The rule preserves the recommendation as a distinct fact. It does not apply to pure preference statements without an explicit recommendation or suggestion.
